review_method: Assistant built-in image inspection through view_image; no separate Hugging Face VLM
target: Red rectangular peg held between the gripper fingers
image_findings: The target is large and visible in both wrist views, with gripper occluding its upper/right portion.
In wrist_2 the peg stays nearly stationary in RGB while the blue board and static table move substantially. This is suitable for testing camera-motion compensation.
The blue board has distinctive holes and the environment has edges useful for static-background correspondences.
The target faces have little texture; tracker persistence is uncertain even when a point remains inside the silhouette.

Registration sheets show holes and varying sensor support in the nearby peg/gripper region. Dark depth-map pixels alone cannot distinguish missing from very near positive depth; quantitative support audit is required.
Side_2 shows only a small target fragment at the top border; its object-motion control is potentially incomplete.
Many unusual distractors are unnecessary. More objects can increase occlusion; the board's distinctive shapes already provide useful static geometry.

quantitative_target_probe.mask_limitation: Observed color component; final eligibility must use actual SAM and all H3 frames.

initial_selection: Retain source-matched episode 5201 for Phase A. It passes initial target visibility/support screening and tests substantial background motion; accept primary geometry only after historical reconstruction and final track audit.
backup_if_geometric_gate_fails: Horizontal red-peg trial n0 has much greater robot rotation diversity in its observed prefix. Any supplemental scene must remain separate and use its own observed-only selection and calibration.
visual_review_limitation: Qualitative source-image review, not instrumented depth registration or material-point ground truth. Full track/forecast review remains pending.
